pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 5.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: ORAL NARRATIVES

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.4: Reading 5.4.1 Intensive Reading: Oral Narratives

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 5.4.1 Intensive Reading: Oral Narratives. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it important to learn about heroes in society?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify heroic characters in legends
2. explain the moral lessons in legends
3. discuss why legends are important in various communities

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 5.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: ORAL NARRATIVES
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 5.4.1 Intensive Reading: Oral Narratives helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 5.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: ORAL NARRATIVES
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify heroic characters in legends

What this means
In this part you learn to identify heroic characters in legends. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify heroic characters in legends.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 5.4.1 Intensive Reading: Oral Narratives”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify heroic characters in legends. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Explain the moral lessons in legends

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the moral lessons in legends. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the moral lessons in legends.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 5.4.1 Intensive Reading: Oral Narratives to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the moral lessons in legends. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Discuss why legends are important in various communities

What this means
In this part you learn to discuss why legends are important in various communities. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: discuss why legends are important in various communities.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can discuss why legends are important in various communities. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 5.4.1 Intensive Reading: Oral Narratives is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 5.4.1 Intensive Reading: Oral Narratives”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify heroic characters in legends)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 5.4.1 Intensive Reading: Oral Narratives to a partner. (skill: explain the moral lessons in legends)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: discuss why legends are important in various communities)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 5.4.1 Intensive Reading: Oral Narratives to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify heroic characters in legends.
3. Practise this skill: explain the moral lessons in legends.
4. Practise this skill: discuss why legends are important in various communities.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 5.4.1 Intensive Reading: Oral Narratives from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 5.4.1 Intensive Reading: Oral Narratives: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Reading 5.4.1 Intensive Reading: Oral Narratives?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important to learn about heroes in society?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 5.4.1 Intensive Reading: Oral Narratives means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify heroic characters in legends.
5. Be able to: explain the moral lessons in legends.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
